antipatterns: app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:31 re-states the revenue expression with DB::raw even though the REVENUE constant at line 15 already holds the same SQL; it could use selectRaw(self::REVENUE)->value() instead
app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:43-82 keeps all three aggregate queries inline in one long return array, and repeats the orders/customers join twice; named private methods would read better
app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:30 docblock promises CarbonImmutable, but $this->date() returns whatever the Date facade is configured for
app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:37-40 calls filled(... ?? null) on every key, which is a bit of ceremony
strengths: Thin invokable controller with a FormRequest that exposes typed filters(); the report logic lives in a dedicated invokable class

Rules use nullable, so empty params such as ?status= or ?from=&to=X fall back to defaults (probe confirmed); uses alpha:ascii plus size:2, Rule::enum, after_or_equal, and uppercases/trims country in prepareForValidation
Modern Laravel throughout: #[Scope] attribute scopes, #[Fillable], casts() method, enum cast, Number::currency
Uses whereIn subqueries, so order count isn't inflated by joins; toBase() avoids hydrating models for aggregate rows; tie-breaking ordering is deterministic
Thorough tests: inclusive date boundaries, orders with no items counted in AOV, empty-string params, array params, thousands separators, the top-5/top-3 caps, and unit_price used over product price

bugs: Empty optional params return 422 instead of being treated as absent. ConvertEmptyStringsToNull turns them into null, and the rules lack nullable, so ?status= gives 422 rather than defaulting to paid. ?from=&to=2026-03-31 and ?country= fail too (probe confirmed). Rules are at app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:22-25
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/SalesReportController.php:13 spreads the filters() array as named arguments into the report, which silently couples array keys to parameter names
app/Http/Requests/SalesReportRequest.php:24 uses plain 'alpha' instead of 'alpha:ascii', so non-ASCII letters pass that rule
app/Reports/BuildSalesReport.php:59-63 calls ->get() on the Eloquent builder, hydrating OrderItem models for raw aggregate rows; toBase() would avoid that
tests/Feature/SalesReportTest.php:30 calls Http::preventStrayRequests() in a test that makes no HTTP calls, which is noise
app/Models/Order.php:16 and app/Models/OrderItem.php:11 leave the foreign keys (customer_id, order_id) out of Fillable, which is inconsistent with the other models
strengths: Clean split into revenuePerCountry, topProducts and topCustomers private methods, plus a typed __invoke signature
Idiomatic Eloquent: whereRelation for the country scope, #[Scope] attributes, clone for builder reuse, orderByDesc on aliases
Expressive factory states (priced(), paid(), placedAt()) and a DataProvider for the invalid-input cases
Tests cover order count not being inflated by multiple items, AOV rounding, spend summed across orders, and the ranking caps

v.rationale: The two implementations are structurally very close: an invokable controller, a FormRequest with filters(), a BuildSalesReport class, attribute scopes, whereIn subqueries and Number::currency. The probes found one real difference. impl-2's rules lack `nullable`, so after ConvertEmptyStringsToNull an empty query param fails validation. `?status=` returns 422 instead of defaulting to paid, and `?from=&to=...` also fails. impl-1 handles all of these as "no filter" and has a test for it (test_empty_filter_values_mean_no_filter). impl-1 also has the stricter `alpha:ascii` country rule, uses toBase() for its aggregate rows, and covers more edge cases in its tests (orders with no items in AOV, thousands formatting, unit_price vs product price). impl-2 has a slightly nicer structure (separate private methods, whereRelation, typed invoke parameters), but the named-argument spread in the controller is fragile, and the empty-param behaviour is a user-facing defect. impl-1 ranks first.
